column3: Close to the Hebrew; “red of garments” is rendered “With dyed garments,” and צֹעֶה (“stooping” or “striding”) “Traveling”; NKJV capitalizes “One” and “His.”
Close to the Hebrew; the verb forms are rendered past, and “spattered” is rendered “sprinkled.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the year of My redemptions” is rendered “the year of My redeemed.”
Close to the Hebrew; “appalled” is rendered “wondered,” and “gave victory” “brought salvation.”
Close to the Hebrew; “their blood” (juice) is rendered “their strength.”
Close to the Hebrew; חַסְדֵי (hesed) is rendered “the lovingkindnesses of,” and “compassion” “mercies.”
Close to the Hebrew; “deliverer” is rendered “Savior.”
NKJV follows the Qere “to Him [there was] affliction” (Kethiv “not”), “He was afflicted,” and capitalizes “the Angel of His Presence.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the spirit of His holiness” is rendered “His Holy Spirit.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “saying,” and follows the reading “shepherd” (singular).
Close to the Hebrew; “caused to go at the right hand” is rendered “led them by the right hand.”
Close to the Hebrew; “gave it rest” is rendered “causes him to rest.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the tumult of Your inward parts” is rendered “The yearning of Your heart.”
Close to the Hebrew; “for” is rendered “Doubtless,” and “from long ago” “from Everlasting.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “it.”
NKJV renders the terse “we have been from long ago, You did not rule them” as “We have become like those of old, over whom You never ruled.”
